paper.title: Analysis of Thompson Sampling for Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandit with Probabilistically Triggered Arms

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with probabilistically triggered arms (CMAB-PTA), semi-bandit feedback
unmapped: Probabilistically triggered base arms: selected super arm triggers a random superset S'(t) of base arms whose outcomes are observed
Expected reward r(S,mu) depends only on S and mu (Assumption 2) and is B-Lipschitz in l1 norm over the triggering set (Assumption 3); nonlinear, non-monotone reward allowed
Learner has an exact computation oracle returning an optimal super arm for any parameter vector (not a linear optimization oracle per se)
Triggering process D^trig and reward function R are known; only outcome distribution D is unknown
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the environment draws a random outcome vector $\pmb{X}(t)$ from a fixed probability distribution $D$ on $[0,1]^m$ independent of the previous rounds... We consider the semi-bandit feedback model, where at the end of round $t$, the learner observes the individual outcomes of the triggered arms... $\text{Reg}(T) := \mathbb{E}[ \sum_{t=1}^T(r(S^*,\pmb{\mu})-r(S(t),\pmb{\mu})) ]$

bound.regime: for all rho in (0,1) and 0 < eps <= 1/sqrt(e) with Delta_S > 2B(k_trig^2+2) eps for all suboptimal S

symbols.B_lip: Lipschitz constant B of the expected reward (Assumption 3)
symbols.G_i: max over suboptimal super arms S whose triggering set contains base arm i of |tilde S|/(Delta_S - 2*B*(k_trig^2+2)*eps)
symbols.p_i: minimum nonzero triggering probability of base arm i
symbols.p_star: minimum nonzero triggering probability over all base arms
symbols.K_trig: maximum triggering set size over all super arms
symbols.k_trig: triggering set size of the optimal super arm S* (tilde k*)
symbols.m_base: number of base arms m (sum_arms ranges over base arms)
symbols.alpha_const: problem-independent constant alpha > 0, independent of T

conditions: Assumption 1: base arm outcomes mutually independent
Assumption 2: expected reward depends only on S and mu
Assumption 3: reward B-Lipschitz in l1 norm over triggering set
tuning: Beta(1,1) priors with Bernoulli trial updates

source.label: t:gapdependent
source.quote: Under Assumptions 1, 2 and 3, for all $D$, the regret of CTS by round $T$ is bounded as follows: \text{Reg}(T) \leq \sum_{i=1}^m \max_{S \in {\cal I} - \text{OPT} :i\in \tilde{S}} \frac{16B^2|\tilde{S}|\log T}{(1-\rho)p_i(\Delta_S - 2B(\tilde{k}^{*2}+2)\varepsilon)} + ... for all $\rho\in(0,1)$, and for all $0 < \varepsilon\leq 1/\sqrt{e}$ such that $\forall S\in\mathcal{I}-\text{OPT}$, $\Delta_S>2B(\tilde{k}^{*2}+2)\varepsilon$

results.notes: Abstract summarises as O(sum_i log T/(p_i Delta_i)). The per-arm max term encoded via declared symbol G_i. Regret is defined via expected reward gaps, so pseudo-regret. CTS does not use T.
